$schema-notes.about: Single source of truth for adamnolle.com. Everything on the site is rendered from this file at build time — edit here, run npm run build, done.
$schema-notes.prose links: profile.intro accepts [label](https://example.com). No other markup is allowed anywhere; all values are escaped.
$schema-notes.projects: source is required, site is optional. A project with both shows VISIT and SOURCE; one with only source shows SOURCE. status LIVE draws a filled marker, anything else an outline.
$schema-notes.hero.windowLabel: Text in the hero terminal title bar. Leave empty to hide it.
$schema-notes.site.tabTitle: Browser tab text. site.title is the longer form used for link previews.
$schema-notes.history[].entries[]: current: true tints the role green and fills the timeline marker. marker: true fills it without the tint.
$schema-notes.header tooltips: Icon links show tooltip on hover and label to screen readers. Omit tooltip and it falls back to label.

projects.name: FileID
projects.description: Point it at a folder and it reads everything inside. Tags by content, clusters faces into people you name once, groups duplicates. Runs entirely on your machine.

projects.name: Document Finder
projects.description: Searches eight open-access research sources plus the web at once, downloads what it finds, pulls the text out, and bundles the lot into a zip you can drop straight into an AI context window.

projects.name: Guitar Tutor
projects.description: Fretboard, chord library, ear trainer, metronome. Every string is synthesized live with a Karplus-Strong model instead of samples, so the whole thing is about 72 KB and works offline.

projects.name: Keyboard Tutor
projects.description: Play the keys, build chords, train your ear, keep time. Works with the computer keyboard or a MIDI controller, generates its own sound, and needs no account or backend.

projects.name: Cube Solver
projects.description: Scramble it or turn faces yourself, then watch it solve from the sticker colors alone. Every solution has to replay back to solved before it counts. Desktop goes to 11×11.

projects.name: LiveBlock
projects.description: An ad blocker that works at the display layer instead of inside the browser, so it covers apps and streams too. Detection runs on device.

projects.name: 3DSeen
projects.description: Guided photogrammetry and LiDAR capture on iPhone, with optional handoff to a paired Mac for the heavy processing. Exports USDZ, OBJ, STL and PLY.

projects.name: Habit Map
projects.description: A pixel-art habit tracker for iPhone, iPad and Watch that does not punish you for missing a day.

projects.name: Web
projects.description: An RSS reader that builds one daily edition and then stops, instead of a feed that never ends. Everything stays in a local SQLite file.

profile.intro: Hi! I'm Adam and I love technology and making things. This site has a little bit about me — you can find more on [webworldwide.online](https://webworldwide.online/).
profile.secondary: In my free time I collect CDs and vinyl. I'm trying to learn the guitar and make beats. I just love pursuing whatever creative endeavor comes to mind.

bullets: Engineer scalable Scala backend services modernizing mission-critical healthcare infrastructure for the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services.
Orchestrate secure CI/CD pipelines that automate testing and deployment, holding to Section 508 compliance and federal security standards.
Optimize high-volume data processing on an Agile team, with rigorous code review and functional programming practice.
Held 99.9% uptime on the P25 radio, microwave and LAN/WAN systems carrying county-wide public safety and emergency response traffic.
Diagnosed hardware faults with RF analysis tools and ran the preventative maintenance that kept downtime off the board.
Coordinated vendors and first responders to deploy resilient comms infrastructure under strict regulatory protocol.
Architected a real-time Location Panel in TypeScript and Angular, wired into CI/CD, giving dispatch live shipment tracking visibility.
Led the Design Systems team: reusable Storybook (CSF3) components and enforced accessibility standards across the internal UI library.
Drove the unit testing push with Karma to raise coverage, and ran the daily Agile ceremonies.
Directed a large student chapter, overseeing nine sub-organizations and the resources behind events, servers and the student storefront.
Secured and allocated over $18,000 to deploy high-performance AI development servers, opening compute access to the whole student body.
Ran major events including the MegaMiner AI coding competition.
Cultivated partnerships with six corporate sponsors, securing financial backing and organizing the professional networking events around them.
Ran event logistics and scheduling as the primary liaison between the chapter and corporate representatives.

cards.title: Hey! 👋
body: Thanks for taking the time to check out my website and learn a little about me. So first let me introduce myself. My name is Adam Nolle. I am a graduate of Missouri University of Science and Technology (or Missouri S&T). I have a B.S. in Computer Science and Computer Engineering with a Minor in Mathematics. From January 2023 to May I was the President of my school's ACM (Association for Computing Machinery) chapter. In my time as President, I brought back our annual MegaMiner event, helped to renovate the second floor CS lounge in our school's Computer Science building, and more!
I currently work at Accenture Federal Services (AFS) full time!

cards.title: (Content) Creator 🎨
body: I love creating things, including digital "content" online for people to enjoy and learn from. I put most of my creative time into my YouTube channel and blog (both named Web World Wide) which are linked in the nav bar above! I love talking about things on my mind.

cards.title: Tech Nerd 🤓
body: If it's technology, I am interested. I have a "Homelab", a 3D Printer, and have built 6 computers (so far, and no, not just for me). This hobby continues to grow for me which is all I can ask for.

cards.title: Music Enjoyer 🎶
body: I enjoy music as most people do 😅. Recently I have started collecting vinyl and CDs of some of my favorite albums (💸). I think supporting artists and owning your media is really important. Also, have you been to a local record store? It's a ton of fun!
I also enjoy making beats in FL Studio and Logic, a hobby I picked up over the summer of 2023. I haven't started posting them yet, but if I do, I will be sure to link them here!
